question: In April 2025, DOT announced funding of two specialised national testbeds for 6G R&D. One focuses on THz communication; which domain does the other explore?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Advanced optical communication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the Department of Telecommunications (**DoT**) announced funding for two specialized **national testbeds** focused on **6G Research and Development (R&D)**.
 
• One of these testbeds is dedicated to **THz (terahertz) communication**, which is a crucial technology for ultra-high-speed data transmission and forms a core aspect of 6G development.
 
• The second testbed focuses on **Advanced optical communication**, a vital area for modern telecommunication systems, enhancing data transmission capabilities over long distances with minimal loss. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Advanced optical communication** involves the use of light for transmitting data through optical fibers, which is essential for achieving the ultra-low latency and high bandwidth requirements of 6G technology.
 
• The government is investing in such testbeds to ensure India remains competitive in next-generation telecommunications technology and to support academic and industrial research in these fields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Advanced optical communication:**

 
 
• This technology uses **optical fibers** to transmit data at high speeds by converting electrical signals into light signals.
 
• It is characterized by **low latency, high bandwidth, and high data integrity**, making it essential for applications like 6G, autonomous vehicles, and IoT (Internet of Things).
 
• It supports key technologies like **Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM)**, which enhances data transmission by using multiple wavelengths of light.
 
• Research in advanced optical communication is paving the way for innovations like **quantum communication** and ultra-secure networks.
 
 
 
• **THz communication:**
 
 
• Terahertz (THz) communication operates in the **0.1–10 THz frequency range** and is a promising technology for ultra-high-speed wireless communication.
 
• It enables data rates of several terabits per second, which is a necessity for 6G networks and beyond.
 
• THz communication is expected to play a role in applications like **holographic communication, real-time AI processing, and immersive virtual reality (VR).**
 
 
 
• **Visible-light communication (VLC):**
 
 
• VLC uses visible light as a medium for wireless communication, often through LEDs.
 
• It is suitable for environments where **radio frequency (RF)** communication faces interference, such as in hospitals or aircraft cabins.
 
• While VLC has its advantages, it is not the focus of the testbed discussed in the question.
 
 
 
• **Quantum key distribution (QKD):**
 
 
• QKD is a **secure communication method** that uses the principles of quantum mechanics to encrypt and transmit data.
 
• It is considered to be unbreakable and is being actively researched for applications in **cybersecurity.**
 
• However, QKD is not the focus of the 6G testbed mentioned in the context of the question.
 
 
 
• **Satellite backhaul:**
 
 
• Satellite backhaul involves using satellites to connect remote areas to the core telecommunication network, providing **internet and cellular services**.
 
• It is especially useful for rural and geographically challenging locations but is not directly related to the testbed for advanced optical communication.
